Header: Erysiphe cichoracearum ( Golovinomyces cichoracearum var. cichoracearum ) powdery mildew disease

Prevention: Plant resistant varieties such as butternut 401, bungle, early butternut
Practice mulching to maintain proper biodiversity and naturally combat invaders.
Practice spacing of 1x1m to increase aeration within the crop
Practice crop rotation with non- host crops such as maize or other cereals for at least 2 years.
Avoid watering the plants using overhead systems to reduce spread of disease
Use a slow-release organic fertilizer to avoid excess nitrogen as young leafy plant parts are susceptible.
Monitoring: Look out for leaves of infected plants with irregular, bright yellow blotches
Look out for leaves with a white to grey powdery growth on upper surface
Look out for sunburn damage on fruit during fruit maturity.
Look out for wilting, distorted and dying leaves
Take action when 2 to 3 leaves are affected with the white to grey powdery deposits on a single plant.
Direct Control: Uproot and burn infected plants in the field to reduce spread of disease to healthy plants
Prune the affected leafy vegetation and weed to remove host plants within the farm.
Spray with sodium bicarbonate (baking powder at the rate of 1 teaspoonful, 1 teaspoonful of vegetable oil and 1 teaspoonful of liquid soap in 4 litres of water).
JIK solution (3 to 5 ml in 1 litre of water) after you have used them on infected plants.
Water early in the morning or after sunset, keeping/aiming the water on the soil, not the leaves.
Trianum-P ( Trichoderma harzianum ) at a rate of 15 g in 5 litres of water or
Trichotech ( Trichoderma asperellum ) at a rate of 2.5g in 20 litres.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB)
Spray mancozeb 80WP 640 g/l, appropriately diluted, and repeat at an interval of 7 to 10 days.
Maximum number of applications per season is 8.
Do not apply more than 19.2 qt per acre per plot.
Apply when plants are in the two leaf stage; repeat at 7 to 10 day intervals.
